about.title: A, B, C: Your First Letters
about.length_note: About 12 minutes: three letters, each with its name, sound, word and a quick check, plus a short opening and a side-by-side review. You can pause or replay any part, so take as long as you like.

say.text: Welcome to Letters A to Z. This is class 1 of 10. Today we meet three letters: A, B and C. Go at your own pace. You can pause or replay whenever you like.

show.text: A, B, C: Your First Letters

say.text: There is no test and no hurry. A wrong answer is just practice. Every class works the same way, in four small steps.

show.text:
1. See the letter
2. Say its name
3. Hear its sound
4. Match a word

say.text: Here is our first letter. Look at the big one: it is an upper case A. It looks like a little tent, or a hill with a bar across the middle. Its name is 'ay'. Say it with me: A.

show.text: A large capital A, like a tent with a bar across the middle, shown next to a small lower case a, which has a round belly and a short stick on the right.

say.text: The small one is lower case a. It has a round belly and a short stick on its right side. Same letter, same name: A. Now the sound. A says 'a', short and quick, like the start of apple. A, a, apple.
There is also a grown-up word for A: address. Ad-dress. Listen for the A sound at the very start. A, a, address.

ask.q: Which word starts with the sound that A makes?
ask.why: Apple starts with the short 'a' sound. The other words start with different sounds.

say.text: Next is B. Its name is 'bee'. Say it: B. Upper case B is a straight line with two bumps on the right side, one on top of the other.

show.text: A large capital B: a tall straight line with two round bumps on its right side. Next to it, a small lower case b.

say.text: Lower case b is a tall stick with one round belly on the right, like a bat standing next to a ball. B makes a quick sound with your lips: press them together, then pop them open. 'b'. B, b, ball.
A grown-up word for B is bread. Bread, bread. Feel your lips pop at the start. B, b, bread.

ask.q: What do your lips do to make the B sound?
wrong: Touch your tongue to your teeth
ask.why: B is made by pressing your lips together and letting them pop apart.

say.text: Now C. Its name is 'see'. Say it: C. Upper case C is a round shape that is open on the right, like a mouth that is open. Lower case c is the very same shape, only smaller.

show.text: A large capital C, a round curve open on the right, next to a small lower case c of the same shape.

say.text: C has two sounds. We start with the common one: 'k', like the start of cat. C, c, cat. A grown-up word is coffee. Coffee, coffee. C, c, coffee.

show.text:
C c = cat (sound: k)
grown-up word: coffee

say.text: Sometimes C says 's', like in city. You do not need that yet. We will meet it again later. For today, C says 'k'.

show.text: Today: C says 'k', as in cat.

ask.q: Which letter says 'k' as in cat?
ask.why: C says 'k' in cat. A says 'a' as in apple, and B says 'b' as in ball.

say.text: Let us put them side by side. Upper case on the left, lower case on the right. Look at each pair. A and a. B and b. C and c. Point to each one as I say it.

show.text:
Upper case | Lower case
A | a
B | b
C | c

say.text: Notice that C and c look almost the same, only the size changes. A and B look different from their small partners. That is why we practise them in pairs.

show.text:
Same shape, different size: C c
Different shape: A a, B b

ask.q: Which one is lower case b?
ask.right: b, the small one with a tall stick and a round belly on the right
wrong: B, the big one with two bumps
a, the small one with a round belly and short stick
ask.why: Lower case b is a tall stick with a round belly on its right side.

say.text: Let us say them all once more. A, a, apple. B, b, ball. C, c, cat. Well done. That is your first three letters.

show.text:
A a: apple (address)
B b: ball (bread)
C c: cat (coffee)

say.text: Next class we meet D, E and F. You can come back to this class any time to practise.
